sections.h2: Who values and who bills property
sections.html:
Edgecombe County's Tax Administration department splits the work between two desks. The assessor appraises property and takes exemption, exclusion and deferment applications. The collector mails bills and goes after unpaid ones. Anyone may look through listing and valuation files from 8:00 AM to 5:00 PM.

  • Taxes paid or owed: the Tax Collector at (252) 641-7810.
  • Value and bill basis questions: the Tax Assessor at (252) 641-7855.
  • Mail for appeals: Edgecombe County Tax Assessor's Office, Attention: Tax Assessor, PO Box 10, Tarboro, NC 27886.

The collector bills for the county itself, 14 fire districts, one drainage district and eight towns: Conetoe, Leggett, Macclesfield, Pinetops, Princeville, Speed, Sharpsburg and Whitakers. Owners in other municipalities get a separate bill from that town or city.

sections.h2: Edgecombe County tax rates by town
sections.html:
The county rate is 0.89 per $100 of value, and each municipality stacks its own rate on top. The rate sheet is labeled 2025, so ask the collector to confirm the figures that will print on your current bill.

The 14 fire districts add their own rates as well, running from 0.07 for Lewis Fire up to 0.145 for Harrison Fire. A $150.00 solid waste fee applies, with a reduced $60.00 version. The county bills the fire districts and the eight small towns itself, so a Pinetops address shows county and town levies on one statement.

Listing opens on the first business day of January and closes January 31. A form that arrives late costs a 10% penalty for each year it was late. Forms for people who have listed before go out by mail in late December.

Houses and land sit in a permanent listing system, so you report only when a building was added, altered or removed. Pulling a building permit is not a substitute for that report. Mobile homes, campers, boats, untagged vehicles, business equipment and appliances in rentals do have to be listed each year.

The person who owned the property on January 1 answers for the whole year, even after a spring sale. Commissioners may stretch the listing season, and someone with good cause can ask in writing for a personal extension before the regular period ends.

sections.h2: When do Edgecombe County tax bills come due?
sections.html:
The due date is September 1, and interest holds off until January 6 under G.S. 105-360. Interest is 2% through the end of January, then three quarters of one percent for every later month or part of a month.

A county or town can set up early payment discounts by resolution before May 1 of the due year, so ask the collector whether one applies when you pay. A payment sent by mail counts as received on its postmark date.

sections.h2: How to challenge your real estate value
sections.html:
Start by calling the assessor at 252-641-7855 or sending in the informal review form. The informal review is open only when your value changed from last year's bill and you are seeing the new number for the first time. A new owner faces the same test.

If the informal result disappoints you, or you did not qualify, you take a formal appeal to the Board of Equalization and Review. The commissioners appoint that panel from residents who know local real estate. It meets in the Administration Building, 201 Saint Andrew Street, Tarboro, and the county publishes a notice each year with the meeting and hearing request dates. Watch the Rocky Mount Telegram for it, or call the assessor.

  • The last revaluation took effect January 1, 2024, and its values stay until the next one.
  • Later swings in the market cannot be weighed in a review.
  • An owner who got word of a change after adjournment has until December 31.
  • Vehicle, business and personal property appeals are due 30 days from the bill date.
  • The next level is the state Property Tax Commission, reached by notice within 30 days of the board's mailed decision (G.S. 105-290).

Exemption, exclusion and deferment applications all go through the assessor. State law offers three homestead paths: an exclusion for elderly or disabled owners, a disabled veteran exclusion and a circuit breaker deferment. Send Form AV-9 to the county assessor. The state takes it through June 1 ahead of the tax year, and the 2026 income limit is $38,800.

Farm and forest owners have a separate path called Present Use Value. It taxes qualifying land at a use schedule and defers the difference. If the land drops out, the county rolls back the year of the change plus three earlier years.

The collector can use foreclosure, sheriff executions, and garnishment of wages, bank accounts and rents. The county keeps a public Tax Foreclosure List that tags each parcel as complaint filed, settlement pending, private sale pending, upset bid period or a posted sale date.

Buyers at these sales leave a 5% deposit, take the property as is, and cannot undo the purchase. For upset bid details, call the Clerk of Court at 252-824-3200 Ext. 2 with the file number. State law gives ten days after a sale report for an upset bid, and an owner can redeem before confirmation by paying taxes, penalties, interest and costs (G.S. 105-374). If your parcel shows up on the list, phone the collector before the sale date.

The collector prepares statements of taxes due for attorneys and real estate professionals. Ask for one before you set the closing date. Deeds need a tax certification before recording unless the attorney preparer statement appears on the instrument, so line that up with your closing attorney too.

  1. Request the statement of taxes due.
  2. Have your closing attorney work out the proration, since January 1 ownership fixes responsibility for the whole year.
  3. Pay any balance from your proceeds at closing.
  4. If the land is in use value, remind the buyer that a new application is needed within 60 days of transfer.

A cash sale skips the lender's payoff and appraisal timing, but the tax statement and deed certification still apply. Our Edgecombe County register of deeds page covers recording fees.

Edgecombe is a rural county with 96.7 residents per square mile over 505.44 square miles of land at the 2020 count. Typical monthly owner costs run $1,252 with a mortgage and $511 without one. Population grew 0.5% from April 2020 to July 2025, and the county has 19,652 households of about 2.44 people each. Those numbers point to a slow, steady market.

faqs.q: What is the Edgecombe County tax rate?
faqs.a: The county rate is 0.89 per $100 of value on its 2025 sheet. Towns and fire districts add their own rates, and a $150.00 solid waste fee applies.

faqs.q: What is the last day to list property in Edgecombe County?
faqs.a: January 31. A form must reach the office or carry a postmark by then, and a late form draws a 10% penalty per year. If the 31st falls on a weekend, the period runs to the next business day.

faqs.q: Where do I start if I think my Edgecombe County value is wrong?
faqs.a: Begin with an informal review: call 252-641-7855 or send the review form. If that does not settle it, file a hearing request with the Board of Equalization and Review before it adjourns.

faqs.q: Is Edgecombe County property revalued each year?
faqs.a: No. State law requires a revaluation at least every eight years, and the last one here took effect January 1, 2024. Between revaluations a house is relisted only when its buildings change.

faqs.q: How can I see whether an Edgecombe County parcel is facing tax foreclosure?
faqs.a: Open the county's Tax Foreclosure List. It shows each parcel's description, township, number, status and file number. For upset bid details, call the Clerk of Court at 252-824-3200 Ext. 2.
